title: Jalapeño Popper Dip
shortDescription: Creamy bacon jalapeño dip with crostini for ten
subtitle: Creamy bacon jalapeño dip with crostini for ten
description: Cream cheese, sour cream, cheddar, bacon, and diced jalapeños bake until bubbly and lightly browned. Serve hot with crostini, tortilla chips, and celery for scooping through the whole game.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Jalapeño Popper Dip in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep jalapeños and bacon
steps.instruction: Deseed and finely dice jalapeños wearing gloves. Crumble cooked bacon into bite-size pieces and measure shredded cheddar so assembly moves fast.

steps.title: Mix the creamy dip base
steps.instruction: Beat cream cheese until smooth, then fold in sour cream, mayonnaise, garlic powder, and onion powder until fully combined and no cream cheese lumps remain.

steps.title: Fold in mix-ins
steps.instruction: Stir in three-quarters of the cheddar, bacon, and jalapeños. Reserve the rest for topping so the surface browns with visible bacon and cheese pockets.

steps.title: Bake until bubbly
steps.instruction: Spread in a buttered 9x13 dish, top with reserved cheese and bacon, and bake at 375°F until edges bubble and center reaches 165°F, about 25–30 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Jalapeño Popper Dip onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve hot
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes so the dip sets slightly. Serve with chips and toasted baguette slices. Keep backup dip warm in the oven if the first dish empties fast.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Jalapeño Popper Dip — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Roast jalapeños first for milder heat and deeper flavor if the crew includes spice-sensitive members.
A tablespoon of cornstarch mixed into the cheddar helps the dip stay thick on hold.
Label 'hot' clearly if using full-strength jalapeños—surprise heat ruins goodwill fast.
tonightSpread: Hot popper dip with chips, crostini, celery sticks, and extra bacon bits.
Cold beer or sparkling water station—rich dip needs something crisp to reset palates.
leftovers: Spread cold dip on tortillas and griddle into quesadillas.
Stuff into hollowed mini peppers and rebake for actual poppers on night two.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Jalapeño popper dip delivers the same spicy-creamy-bacon hit as stuffed peppers with a fraction of the prep. One casserole dish feeds the hall and stays hot in a low oven.
mealPrepNotes: Dice and deseed jalapeños wearing gloves. Cook bacon ahead. Assemble dip in a buttered dish up to 24 hours ahead and bake from cold, adding 10 minutes.
